question: By whom has the term 'bargaining federalism' been used?
solution: Morris Jones coined the term while analyzing the politics of the 1950s and 60s, where states bargained with the Center for their demands.

question: Which subject was not transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act?
solution: Five subjects – education, forests, weights and measures, wildlife conservation and administration of justice – were brought into the concurrent list through the 42nd amendment in 1976.

question: In which schedule are the details of allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha given?
solution: The Fourth Schedule decides how much representation each state will have in the Upper House of Parliament. This allocation is mainly done on the basis of the population of the state.

question: 'Gram Sabha' and 'Nagar Sabha' are examples of which type of democracy?
solution: The objective of local bodies is to take administration to the doorstep of the public.

question: What is the characteristic of concurrent list?
options: No one can make any law
Only the Center can make laws
Both the Center and the State can make laws.
solution: The concurrent list includes subjects like education, forests, marriage and divorce. It originally had 47 subjects which has now increased to 52.

question: What is the order of 'L' and 'D' in the trick to remember the '12 Schedules' of the Indian Constitution?
options: L (Land) is ninth and D (Defection) is tenth
D is before and L is after
solution: TEARS OF OLD PM - L (Land) is the ninth letter and D (Defection) is the tenth. This trick also reflects the sequence of historical development.

question: Why are 'All India Services' (IAS/IPS) considered a unitary feature?
options: Because only Hindi is spoken in them
Because this service ends after retirement
Because they are only in Delhi
Because they are selected by the Center but they work in the states
solution: All India services help maintain the unity of the country, but state governments often consider this an interference in their autonomy.

question: Why are judges included in the 'Oath and Affirmation' (Third Schedule)?
options: Because it is an old tradition
To ensure the independence and impartiality of the judiciary, the oath reminds them of the dignity of the Constitution and to act without any bias.
So that they remain under the ministers
solution: Judges take an oath that they will administer justice "without fear or favour, affection or ill-will". It is essential for Indian democracy.

question: What powers do 'Autonomous District Councils' (ADCs) have under the Sixth Schedule?
options: What powers does it have? A) Legislative, Judicial and Executive Powers
solution: The Sixth Schedule provides extensive self-governance to the tribal areas of the North-East so that their culture and traditions can be protected.

question: Why is English not included in the 'Official Languages' (Eighth Schedule)?
options: Because the Constituent Assembly had given priority only to languages ​​of Indian origin
Because there was space for only 22 languages, the number of languages ​​could be increased, but the proposal to include English has not been passed yet.
Because English is not spoken in India
solution: Inclusion in the Eighth Schedule enables a language to receive the Sahitya Akademi Award and other government benefits. Rajasthani and Bhojpuri are also waiting to be included in this list.

question: Why has 'Defence' been kept only in the Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution?
options: National security requires a unified command and policy
Because the army was near the center during the British period, independent India kept defense as the central subject as per its needs.
Because states do not have weapons
solution: Entry No. 1 and 2 of the Union List mention defense and armed forces. This ensures that India's security system works in the same direction.

question: What is the benefit to small traders by keeping 'Insolvency' in the concurrent list?
options: They can seek relief under Central or State laws
They never have to repay the loan
solution: By being in the concurrent list, local business organizations can also get assistance from the states.

question: What is the evaluative function of 'Judiciary' according to the Indian Constitution?
options: To see whether the laws made by the legislature are constitutional or not is called the power of Judicial Review.
solution: The judiciary ensures that neither Parliament nor the government abuses its powers.

question: 'Procedure established by law' and 'Responsive Government' are the characteristics of which system?
options: In communist system, there is centralization of powers in a single party.
solution: In India, the Parliament can ask questions of the government, bring forward proposals and controls it through the budget.

question: What is meant by the mixture of rigidity and flexibility in the Indian Constitution?
options: The Constitution can never be changed
Every part of the Constitution can be changed by a simple majority
Some provisions are amended by simple majority and some by special majority
Only the Judiciary can change the Constitution
solution: The Indian Constitution is neither completely rigid nor completely flexible. Parts of it can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament (flexible), while some important provisions require a special majority and the consent of half the states (rigid).

question: If two or more States request it (Article 252), what will be the law made by the Parliament?
options: It will be valid only for 1 year
It will automatically apply to all states
It will apply only to the requesting states and they will not be able to change it themselves
solution: Article 252 is used when states want a uniform law on a common subject. For example, some laws related to water pollution or wildlife conservation.

question: 'Adoption and Succession' is a subject of which list?
options: It is subject only to religious laws
solution: Entry 5 of the Concurrent List deals with marriage, divorce, protection of infants and minors and succession.

question: Whose responsibility is 'urban poverty alleviation' included in the Twelfth Schedule (M - Municipalities)?
options: Only the central government funds, but the implementation is done by the municipalities.
solution: The 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to municipalities and assigned a list of 18 functions so that urban governance could be democratic.

question: What is the meaning of federalism?
options: States act as agents of the central government
Only the central government has all the powers
Existence of more than one level of government in the country
Having only one level of government
solution: Federalism implies decentralization of powers. There are three levels of government in India: Centre, State and local bodies. State governments are not mere representatives of the Centre, but their powers are secured by the Constitution.

question: Who has the power to decide the standards of 'Weights and Measures'?
options: Both the Center and the State have it under the Concurrent List.
solution: The 42nd Amendment transferred several subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List to bring uniformity at the national level.

question: 'Conservation of wild animals and birds' is currently included in which list?
solution: The purpose of placing wildlife conservation in the concurrent list was to create better coordination between the Center and the states to protect the environment.

question: Who generally makes laws on subjects in the State List?
solution: There were originally 66 subjects in the state list which have now reduced to 61. Public order, local self-government and fisheries are its examples.

question: What is the main difference between written constitution and unwritten constitution?
options: There is a system of unwritten constitution in India
Written constitutions are easier to amend
Written constitution is compiled systematically whereas unwritten one is not.
solution: Written constitutions, such as the Constitution of India, have a settled structure and are difficult to change. Whereas an unwritten constitution, such as the British Constitution, is not formally compiled and can be easily amended.

question: By which organ is the 'Rule of Law' ensured in India?
solution: Rule of law means that no person is above the law. This is the basis of democracy.

question: Which power do not the States have in relation to 'Weights and Measures'?
options: Changing national standards on its own
This power rests with the states to punish those who violate the rules.
solution: Differences in standards can erode business and consumer confidence, so 'standards' are under centralized control.

question: 'Prison' and 'Reformation Home' are subjects of which list?
solution: Entry 4 of the State List mentions prisons and correctional institutions.

question: What is the biggest advantage of the Indian Constitution being 'written'?
options: Clear division of powers and reduction in disputes
It does not require a lawyer
It is very heavy and detailed
solution: A written constitution guarantees civil rights and limits the powers of the government, preventing arbitrary rule.

question: What are the consequences of not taking the 'Oath' (Third Schedule)?
options: A person may be jailed, but not jailed, but he becomes ineligible for office.
A person can become the Prime Minister
A person cannot assume charge of his post
solution: Even after winning the election, unless an MP or MLA takes oath, he cannot participate in the proceedings of the House.

question: 'Maithili' language is mainly spoken in which state and is included in the Eighth Schedule?
solution: The inclusion of Maithili was to give national recognition to the cultural identity of that region.

question: What name has Granville Austin given to Indian federalism?
solution: Cooperative federalism means that the Center and the states act as complements to each other. Granville Austin had placed the making of the Indian Constitution and its functioning in this category.

question: Why have 'Maithili' and 'Dogri' not got the status of classical languages, even though they are in the Eighth Schedule?
options: Because the government doesn't like them
Because they do not fully meet the ancient standards of classicism (ancient literature of 1500-2000 years)
Because they are from North India
solution: Currently 11 languages ​​(including new changes as of 2024) have classical status, representing India's most ancient literary traditions.

question: Can Ninth Schedule laws still be challenged in court?
options: Only with the permission of the President
Yes, if they violate fundamental rights or the basic structure of the Constitution
Only with the consent of the Parliament
No, these laws are completely beyond judicial review
solution: The Ninth Schedule was initially a safeguard, but with the advent of the principle of 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution, its full protection has been lost.

question: Who has the power to decide the standards of 'Weights and Measures'?
options: Both the Center and the State have it under the Concurrent List.
solution: The 42nd Amendment transferred several subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List to bring uniformity at the national level.

question: 'Local Self-Government' is a subject of which list?
solution: Local self-government gained more importance after the 73rd and 74th amendments, but it still comes under Entry No. 5 of the State List.

question: What is the main objective of the Seventh Schedule?
options: Division of powers between the Union and the States
solution: The Seventh Schedule is the basis of the federal structure. It makes it clear on which subjects only the Center will make laws, on which the states and on which both will work together.

question: What modifications are the 'Salt' and 'BDSM' tricks associated with?
solution: Through these tricks, students can easily remember the year of addition of languages ​​and amendment number in competitive exams.

question: Why is construction of 'roads and bridges' included in the subjects of 'Municipality' (Twelfth Schedule)?
options: Because the Center cannot build roads
So that toll tax can be collected
solution: To make the urban administration self-reliant, they have been assigned 18 important tasks so that they can plan according to the needs of their city.

question: What is the main objective behind Single Citizenship?
options: Making it difficult to grant citizenship to foreigners
To promote unity and integrity of the country
solution: The US has dual citizenship (country and state separate), but India, like the UK, has adopted single citizenship to reduce regionalism.

question: Who makes laws on the subjects of 'Union Public Service Commission' (UPSC)?
options: Who makes laws on the subjects of? A) Parliament (Union List)
solution: Entry 70 of the Union List mentions the Public Services and All India Services of the Union.

question: How many levels of government exist in India?
solution: The Indian federal system has three levels. At the top is the Union or Central government, followed by state governments, and at the grassroots level, local self-government functions as panchayats and municipalities.

question: What makes India a combination of 'federal' and 'unitary' characteristics?
solution: According to Dr. Ambedkar, the Constitution can be molded into both federal and unitary moulds, depending on the demand of the time.

question: What is the place of 'Bengali' among the new classical languages ​​announced in 2024?
options: It is only a modern language
It is spoken only in Bengal
It represents one of India's richest literary traditions.
solution: Along with Bengali, Marathi and Assamese also got this distinction in 2024, which shows the growing importance of regional languages.

question: What is the First Schedule of the Indian Constitution related to?
options: Names of States and Union Territories and their Territorial Jurisdictions
Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha
solution: The First Schedule defines the geographical structure of India. Whenever a new state is formed or the boundary of a state changes, the First Schedule is amended.

question: What path has India adopted between 'Parliamentary Sovereignty' (British Model) and 'Judicial Supremacy' (American Model)?
options: A middle path and coordination between the two
solution: This is called 'constitutional balance'. Parliament makes laws and the judiciary sees whether those laws are within the Lakshman Rekha or not.

question: What did the '22nd Part' of the Indian Constitution originally represent?
options: Short title, commencement, authorized text in Hindi and repeal
solution: Presently the number of parts has increased to 25 as new parts like 4A, 9A, 9B and 14A have been added by amendments.

question: What is the function of 'Tribal Advisory Council' mentioned in the Fifth Schedule?
options: Advising the Governor on the welfare of Scheduled Tribes
Sending reports to the Central Government
solution: The Tribal Advisory Council consists of a maximum of 20 members, of whom three-fourths should be representatives of the Scheduled Tribes in the State Assembly.

question: Why was the rule of 'Split' in the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule) changed later?
options: Because it was too flexible it was made rigid to prevent instability caused by flexibility.
Because it was being misused for mass defection, the exemption for division of 1/3 members was abolished by the 91st Amendment (2003).
Because political parties were dying out, rules were tightened to strengthen the parties.
solution: Now only 'merge' of two-thirds of its members into another party is exempted from defection, not individual or small group defection.

question: What does 'O' mean in the 'TEARS OF OLD PM' trick?
solution: Through this trick all the 12 schedules can be remembered in sequence. T-Territory, E-Emoluments, A-Affirmation, R-Rajya Sabha, S-Scheduled Areas, O-Other Scheduled Areas, F-Federal, O-Official Languages, L-Land, D-Defection, P-Panchayat, M-Municipalities.

question: Which schedule was added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, 1992?
solution: The Eleventh Schedule provides constitutional status to local self-government in rural areas. In this, 29 subjects have been included for the work of Panchayats.

question: 'Foreign Affairs' and 'War and Peace' come under which list?
solution: The subjects of the Union List are related to the sovereignty and integrity of India. Airways, railways and sea routes are also part of this.

question: The Sixth Schedule provides for the administration of tribal areas of which four states?
solution: The Sixth Schedule provides for the formation of District Councils for Tribal Autonomy in four specific states of the North-East. These councils also have legislative and judicial powers.

question: What does Ninth Schedule (L) mean according to the 'Tears of Old PM' trick?
solution: The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Amendment (1951) to keep socio-economic reforms free from legal constraints.

question: For how long can Parliament make laws on subjects in the State List during national emergency?
options: Till 6 months after the emergency is lifted
solution: During emergency the structure of India becomes unitary. Parliament gets the power to make laws on the State List, but this power is temporary.

question: What effect do 'emergency provisions' have on the federal structure of the Constitution?
options: The federal structure temporarily changes to a unitary one
solution: Emergency (Articles 352, 356, 360) is a unique feature of the Indian Constitution that gives priority to national security in times of crisis.

question: What should be the minimum number of members in the Tribal Advisory Council under 'Schedule 5'?
solution: The main objective of the Tribal Council is to advise the Governor on the customs and traditions of the tribes and their socio-economic development.

question: The idea of ​​'Concurrent List' of the Seventh Schedule is inspired by which country? (PDF Note: General Knowledge)
solution: The Concurrent List is a great example of cooperation and coordination between the Center and the states.

question: Why has 'Police' been included in the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution?
options: Because it was the same during the British period, many British traditions have been changed, this has been kept for administrative convenience.
Because the states had demanded it
Because maintaining law and order is a local responsibility
solution: Police and public order are the most important subjects in the State List. However, in union territories like Delhi, the police are under the Centre.

question: Which three languages ​​were added by the 71st Constitutional Amendment (1992)?
solution: In 1992, three languages ​​were recognized simultaneously. Konkani of Goa, Manipuri of Manipur and Nepali are also spoken in many parts of India.

question: What is meant by 'Integrated Judiciary'?
options: Judiciary being subordinate to the Parliament
Separate independent courts for the Center and the States
A single judicial pyramid for the entire country with the Supreme Court at the top
solution: Integrated judiciary is a unitary feature. This means that the same interpretation of law applies equally throughout the country and decisions of lower courts can be challenged in higher courts.

question: What is the main difference between 'Supremacy of the Constitution' and 'Parliamentary Sovereignty'?
options: Supremacy means rule of the military
The supremacy of the Constitution limits the powers of the Parliament, but not the sovereignty.
Sovereignty means the rule of the king
solution: The powers of Parliament in India are 'defined' and 'limited' by the Constitution.

question: What is the current status of classical languages ​​in India?
options: Their number has increased after the addition of new languages ​​in 2024.
Only Hindi is a classical language
solution: The status of classical language is given to those languages ​​whose history is at least 1500-2000 years old. Tamil was the first classical language.

question: Which of the following is a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
solution: Federal characteristics include written constitution, supremacy of the constitution, independent judiciary, bicameral legislature and separation of powers. These features protect the autonomy of the states.

question: Why is 'supremacy of the Constitution' considered an essential condition of federal system?
options: So that the judiciary gets salary
So that only the President remains powerful
So that the Parliament can do anything
So that both the Center and the States remain within their boundaries
solution: If the Constitution was not supreme, the Center could take away the powers of the states at any time.

question: What is the meaning of 'Executive' according to the Indian Constitution?
options: The organ that creates new states
The organ that protects the Constitution
The organ that implements the laws made by the legislature
The organ that appoints judges of the Supreme Court
solution: The executive is answerable to the legislature. Its main function is to ensure that the decisions of Parliament are implemented on the ground.

question: 'Prevention of Cruelty to Animals' is the subject of which list?
options: It is not included in any list
solution: Being in the concurrent list, the central government has been able to make laws like 'Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act', which are implemented by the states.

question: What does 'unified and independent judiciary' mean?
options: Courts are only for the rich
Judiciary works closely with the police
The judiciary is free from outside interference and the Supreme Court is above the lower courts
solution: Judiciary in India is the protector of the Constitution. It can issue 'writs' and quash government orders if fundamental rights are violated.

question: When was education transferred from State List to Concurrent List?
options: In 1976, through the 42nd Amendment, the Center was also given the power to make laws on education so that there is national uniformity in the standards of education.
solution: With education included in the Concurrent List, the Central Government was able to make all India laws like 'Right to Education' (RTE).

question: What is the advantage of keeping 'Electricity' in the concurrent list?
options: The Center can decide the infrastructure standards and the states can look after the distribution
Only the Center can decide the electricity bill
So that electricity is available only with the permission of the Parliament
solution: Entry 38 of the Concurrent List covers electricity. The Electricity Act, 2003 is a major law made by the Parliament.

question: Whose primary responsibility is 'Public Health and Sanitation'?
solution: Public health is mentioned in entry number 6 of the State List of the Seventh Schedule. States decide how they will manage health services.

question: 'Foreign Affairs' and 'War and Peace' come under which list?
solution: The subjects of the Union List are related to the sovereignty and integrity of India. Airways, railways and sea routes are also part of this.

question: What does it mean to be a 'republic' in the Indian Constitution?
options: The head of the country (President) is elected, not hereditary
solution: The word Republic guarantees that no position in India is reserved for any particular family. Election is held for the highest post.

question: Where is the concept of 'Welfare State' found in the Indian Constitution?
solution: Welfare state means that the government is not limited to police and security only, but it is also responsible for education, health and poverty alleviation.

question: To whom is the 'Council of Ministers' collectively responsible in the Indian parliamentary system?
options: There is personal responsibility towards the President, but collective responsibility is towards the Parliament (Lok Sabha).
solution: This is the most important principle of parliamentary democracy, which ensures that the executive remains under the control of the representatives of the public.

question: Why were 'independent bodies' (like Election Commission, CAG) made a part of the Constitution in India?
solution: Bodies like the Election Commission, CAG and Union Public Service Commission are considered the 'protectors' of the Indian Constitution.

question: How does 'Article 356' (President's Rule) promote unity?
options: The Center directly takes over the governance of the state and the assembly can be dissolved or suspended
It gives more funds to the states
solution: Dr. Ambedkar had called it a 'dead letter', but in practical politics it has been used many times to challenge the federal rights of the states.

question: What is the main argument for keeping 'Agriculture' in the state list?
options: Center is not interested in agriculture
Because there is no tax on agriculture
Diversity of local climate and soil of agriculture
Farmers know only the state government
solution: Agriculture is mentioned in entry 14 of the State List. However, the Center can also influence the agricultural sector through certain aspects such as trade and commerce.

question: What is the role of States under 'Weights and Measures' (Entry 33A, Concurrent List)?
options: Implementing measurement systems as per the standards set by the Centre.
solution: This subject is important for the protection of consumer rights so that fraud in weights and measures can be prevented.

question: What is the importance of 'Fisheries' in the State List?
options: Managing local water resources and the livelihoods of coastal communities
solution: Entry 21 of the State List covers fisheries. Inland fisheries are entirely under the control of the states.

question: What is necessary to attain the status of 'classical language'?
options: The language should be of North India only
The language should contain only modern words
The literature of the language should be very ancient and original
The language should be spoken only by the government
solution: The government makes special grants and establishes centers of study in universities for the preservation of classical languages.

question: What is an example of the Indian Constitution being 'rigid'?
options: Consent of half the states is mandatory for amending the federal structure of the Constitution.
solution: A very difficult path has been adopted for some amendments under Article 368 so that the basic spirit of the Constitution is protected.

question: Which of the following subjects is included in the Union List?
solution: The Union List contains subjects on which a uniform policy is required throughout the country, such as defence, banking and foreign policy.

question: What is the correct trick for the languages ​​added by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment (2003)?
solution: The 92nd amendment of 2003 added four languages ​​simultaneously, increasing the total number of languages ​​from 18 to 22.

question: What type of characteristic is the appointment of the Governor by the Centre?
solution: The Governor is appointed by the President. This post acts as a link between the Center and the states, but at times it is also considered against federal autonomy.

question: What does the supremacy of the Indian Constitution mean?
options: Parliament, Executive and Judiciary are all subject to the Constitution
Parliament is supreme and it can do anything
The President is the center of real power
solution: The supremacy of the Constitution is a federal characteristic. This ensures that the division of powers remains stable and no organ exceeds its limits.

question: What happens to the subjects in the Union List in case of 'armed rebellion' or 'external aggression'?
options: States can also make laws on them
The Center continues to have the power to make and enforce special laws on them
Only the United Nations can intervene
solution: In times of crisis, the entire machinery of the country operates from a single center so that decisions can be taken quickly.

question: What is the third schedule related to?
options: The division of powers between the Union and the States is done through three lists in the Seventh Schedule.
Formats of oath and affirmation to be taken by various candidates
solution: The Third Schedule ensures that persons holding public office take an oath of allegiance to the Constitution. It includes Union Ministers, Ministers of State, Judges and CAG.

question: Who said 'Union with centralized tendency'?
solution: Ivor Jennings believed that the Indian Constitution gave so many powers to the Center that it appeared to be at odds with the traditional principles of federalism.

question: Who gives financial power to local bodies in 'three-tier government'?
options: By extorting money from the public
State Government on the recommendation of the State Finance Commission
They can print the notes themselves
solution: Without financial autonomy, local self-government would have remained only in name, hence financial provisions were also made in the 73rd Amendment.

question: If both the Center and the State make laws on any subject in the Concurrent List, whose law will prevail?
options: Both the laws will be repealed
The decision will be taken by the public through referendum
solution: There is co-existence of powers in the concurrent list, but the supremacy of the Center remains. If the state law gets the assent of the President, it can remain in effect in that particular state.

question: What do the 'features' of the Indian Constitution emphasize?
options: Balance of flexibility and rigidity in governance
Only on the influence of the judiciary
Only on the supremacy of the Centre
solution: The Indian Constitution is not just a legal book, but it is a social instrument to preserve the democratic values ​​and diversity of the country.

question: What can Parliament do to enforce international treaties (Article 253)?
options: Can make laws only in those states which are affected
It is mandatory to take permission from the states to make laws.
Parliament can make laws on any subject for the whole of India. In this situation, the Parliament does not require the consent of any state.
Can make laws only on subjects in the Union List
solution: The Parliament has been given supreme legislative power to fulfill the promises and agreements made by the Government of India at the global level, so that the federal structure does not become a hindrance in international relations.

question: By which amendment was the word 'secular' added to the Indian Constitution? (PDF Reference: Mini Constitution)
solution: India's model of secularism is 'positive', where the state respects all religions equally.

question: Why has 'Gambling and Betting' been included in the State List?
options: Because it's only a local game
Because states can control it according to their society and law and order
Because it brings a lot of revenue to the states
Because the Center considers it morally wrong
solution: Entry 34 of the State List covers gambling and betting. For this reason its rules are different in different states.

question: On what basis are 'Rajya Sabha seats' (Fourth Schedule) allotted?
options: All states are given equal seats
Based on the population of the states
Based on the area of ​​the state
solution: Population-based representation ensures that voices are heard according to the number of people in Parliament.

question: What does 'Schedule' represent in the Indian Constitution?
options: Detailed explanations and lists of articles of the Constitution
List of laws that have been repealed
solution: The Schedules make the Constitution more clear and detailed. For example, the Seventh Schedule explains the division of powers in detail through lists.

question: Through which list do 'Local Bodies' (Panchayats & Municipalities) function?
options: Only by order of the Governor
Through the entries in the State List and the Eleventh/Twelfth Schedule,
According to the rules of the United Nations
solution: The objective of local self-government is to ensure access of power to the last person.

question: Who has the power to create 'All India Services' (Entry 70)?
options: The President only issues the notification, the legislative power rests with the Parliament.
solution: This is another special power of the Rajya Sabha which maintains balance in the federal structure.

question: 'Adoption and Succession' is a subject of which list?
options: It is subject only to religious laws
solution: Entry 5 of the Concurrent List deals with marriage, divorce, protection of infants and minors and succession.

question: What is the meaning of 'Entry' in the context of legislative lists?
options: Name of amendment in the Constitution:
A specific subject or item given within the lists
solution: Like Entry 1 of the Union List is 'Defence'. Subtle division of powers has been done through entries.

question: Salary and allowances of which of the following are not mentioned in the Second Schedule?
options: Provisions regarding the salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
solution: The Second Schedule deals with the achievements of persons holding constitutional offices. It consists of the President, Vice President (as Chairman), Governor, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and judges.

question: 'Oath' (Third Schedule) and 'Allocation of Seats' (Fourth Schedule) are important for the stability of which House?
options: For both the Parliament and the Legislative Assembly, these procedures are the basis for the initiation and representation of legislative business.
solution: Without oath, no member can function and without allocation of seats, formation of Houses is not possible.

question: What is the reason for placing 'Marriage and Divorce' in the Concurrent List?
options: Because the Center receives revenue from marriage registration there is no major Centre-State issue.
Because it is only religious matter
Because the states do not have the power to make laws on this
So that there remains some uniformity in family laws across the country
solution: The concurrent list includes those subjects which require local diversity as well as national coordination.

question: Who bears the expenses of conducting 'Census'?
options: It operates from general tax revenue by collecting taxes from the public.
solution: The census is the world's largest administrative and statistical exercise, conducted every 10 years.

question: How many functional subjects are given for municipalities in the Twelfth Schedule?
solution: The Twelfth Schedule was added by the 74th Amendment. It deals with urban administration such as sanitation, water supply and construction of roads.

question: Bicameralism is a part of which schedule or feature in the Indian Constitution?
options: It is mandatory only for the states
solution: Lok Sabha represents the people and Rajya Sabha represents the states. That is why the bicameral system is considered an important part of the federal structure.

question: Which statement is most accurate about the nature of the Indian Constitution?
options: States have the freedom to secede from the Union
Only union of states without any center
solution: India is called a 'union with a strong centre'. The constitution has features of federalism (written constitution, separation of powers) as well as unitary features (single citizenship, appointment of the governor).

question: 'Conservation of wild animals and birds' is currently included in which list?
solution: The purpose of placing wildlife conservation in the concurrent list was to create better coordination between the Center and the states to protect the environment.

question: What does it mean to be a 'republic' in the Indian Constitution?
options: The head of the country (President) is elected, not hereditary
solution: The word Republic guarantees that no position in India is reserved for any particular family. Election is held for the highest post.

question: Which part of the '25 parts' of the Indian Constitution is related to Panchayat? (PDF Reference: Part Number)
solution: There is a clear classification of subjects in different parts of the Constitution. Part 9 (Panchayats) and Part 9A (Municipalities) are the basis of local self-government.

question: Which main laws were made under 'Land Reforms' (Ninth Schedule)?
options: Abolition and consolidation of the Zamindari system
solution: The Ninth Schedule helped bring major social changes in rural areas of India, although it was also controversial.

question: Why are 'Banking' and 'Insurance' included in the Union List?
options: Because foreign investment comes only through the Centre
Central control is necessary to make the banking system safe and reliable, for financial stability and uniformity throughout the country.
Because states do not have banks
Because these happen only in cities
solution: Subjects like currency, banking, insurance and stock market are the backbone of the national economy, hence these are placed under the jurisdiction of the Parliament (Union List).

question: Apart from 'Agriculture' and 'Land Reforms', which function does Panchayats have under the Eleventh Schedule (P - Panchayat)?
solution: There are 29 subjects in the Eleventh Schedule which are directly related to the social and economic development of villages.

question: Which of the following is considered a unitary feature of the Constitution?
solution: The purpose of unitary characteristics is to maintain the unity and integrity of the country. It includes points like single citizenship, appointment of the Governor by the Centre, integrated judiciary and flexible constitution.

question: Why has 'Airways' been included in the 'Union List' of the Seventh Schedule?
options: Uniform regulation and security is necessary for international and national air transportation.
Because states do not have pilots
Because only the center buys airplanes
solution: The Ministry of Civil Aviation (Centre) controls airports and flights throughout the country.

question: Why are 'Banking' and 'Insurance' included in the Union List?
options: Because foreign investment comes only through the Centre
Because states do not have banks
Because these happen only in cities
Central control is necessary to make the banking system safe and reliable, for financial stability and uniformity throughout the country.
solution: Subjects like currency, banking, insurance and stock market are the backbone of the national economy, hence these are placed under the jurisdiction of the Parliament (Union List).

question: Why is the name of 'Vice President' not mentioned in the context of salary in the Second Schedule of the Constitution?
options: Because the President decides their salary
Because he gets salary as 'Chairman of Rajya Sabha'
Because they are not members of the government
solution: The Second Schedule mentions "Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha", which clarifies how the Vice President is paid.

question: Anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule) does not apply to whom?
options: When an independent member joins a party after elections, it also comes under the category of defection.
When two-thirds of the members merge with another party, it is considered a legal merger, not defection.
When a member leaves his party
When a nominated member joins a party after 6 months, it is also considered as defection.
solution: This law prevents switching parties for personal gain, but allows ideological mergers of larger political groups.

question: The second 'O' in the 'Tears of Old PM' trick (Official Languages) represents which schedule?
solution: The order of letters in the trick is as per the order of the schedules. The Eighth Schedule is dedicated to languages.

question: What effect does having a 'single constitution' have on the states?
options: States are not allowed to make their own separate constitutions
States cannot make laws of their own free will
States only follow the orders of the Centre. Under normal circumstances, states are autonomous.
solution: Jammu and Kashmir earlier had its own constitution, but after 2019, now only one constitution is effective in the whole of India.

question: What do the subjects like 'Fisheries' and 'Drinking Water' included in the Eleventh Schedule (Panchayati Raj) represent?
options: Control of local communities over their resources
Only methods of tax collection are subject to development and service delivery.
Special rights of the state government
solution: The objective of the 73rd Amendment was 'democratic decentralization'. The list of 29 subjects empowers Panchayats for local development.

question: What is the historical significance of 'Pali' and 'Prakrit' declared as classical languages ​​in 2024?
options: These are the main languages ​​of ancient Buddhist and Jain religious texts.
These are the languages ​​of modern technology
These are spoken only in South India
solution: Giving classical status to Pali and Prakrit is like giving respect to the ancient linguistic heritage of India.

question: Which of these languages ​​has not been newly added as a classical language in 2024?
solution: In 2024, the Government of India recognized five new languages ​​– Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali as classical languages ​​to promote linguistic heritage.

question: What powers do 'Autonomous District Councils' (ADCs) have under the Sixth Schedule?
options: What powers does it have? A) Legislative, Judicial and Executive Powers
solution: The Sixth Schedule provides extensive self-governance to the tribal areas of the North-East so that their culture and traditions can be protected.

question: What is the impact of placing 'Education' in the concurrent list?
options: Only Hindi is taught in schools
Center can now run national schemes like 'Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan'
States can no longer make laws on education
solution: Concurrency of education has helped in developing a common educational framework (like CBSE or National Education Policy) in India.

question: Which tendency of India to give 'Residual Powers' to the Parliament reflects?
solution: In America, residual powers are with the states, but India adopted the Canadian model so that the union remains strong. Cyber ​​crime and space research are examples of this.

question: What is the benefit of keeping 'Railways' in the Union List in the Seventh Schedule?
options: Because coal is near the centre, trains also run on electricity and diesel, this is an issue of administrative convenience.
So that the states do not earn
The track network and ticketing system remains the same throughout the country
solution: Entry 22 of the Union List is 'Railways'. It is the largest public enterprise under direct control of the Centre.

question: How many languages ​​were originally included in the Eighth Schedule?
solution: The Eighth Schedule was created keeping in mind the linguistic diversity of India. Currently it has 22 languages, the last amendment to which was made by the 92nd Amendment.

question: What is the significance of 'Census' included in the Union List?
options: This is the function of the Election Commission
Gives states the power to count their own population
It is only a concurrent subject
It is the responsibility of the center for the demographic data of the entire country.
solution: Comes under census entry number 69 (Union List). It provides the basis for distribution and delimitation of the country's resources.

question: 'How. Why did Hweer not call the Indian Constitution a 'unitary state'?
options: Because there is only one language
Because there is no king in India
Because here the states have their own independent constitutional powers
solution: Hewer used the term 'quasi-federal' to indicate balance, not outright support of any one party.

question: 'Local Self-Government' is a subject of which list?
solution: Local self-government gained more importance after the 73rd and 74th amendments, but it still comes under Entry No. 5 of the State List.

question: The 'Strong Centre' model of the Indian Constitution has been taken from which country?
solution: The main reason for having a strong center was the diversity of India and the instability at the time of partition, so that the country could be kept united.

question: 'Article 244' of the Constitution is related to which schedule?
solution: Articles 244 and 244A provide autonomy and special protection to areas with tribal population.

question: What is the Tenth Schedule related to?
options: Disqualification of MPs and MLAs on grounds of defection
solution: The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985. This is commonly known as the 'anti-defection law'.

question: What does 'K' mean in 'Salt' (Hindi Trick of 71st Amendment Languages)?
solution: The 'salt' trick is easy: Na - Nepali, M - Manipuri, K - Konkani. All three were part of the 71st amendment.

question: 'Population control and family planning' is the subject of which list?
solution: The Center provides financial support and guidelines to make family planning and population control effective, while the states implement it on the ground.

question: Under Article 249, on what basis can Rajya Sabha give power to Parliament to make laws on the State List?
options: On the recommendation of the Governor
On the request of the State Government
solution: Article 249 is a special power of the Rajya Sabha. The resolution passed under this is valid for one year and can be extended again and again.

question: How many times has the word 'Federal' been used in the 'Preamble' of the Indian Constitution?
options: At the end of the Preamble, there are words like liberty, equality and fraternity.
solution: Dr. Ambedkar preferred the word 'Union' to make it clear that the Indian Union was not the result of any agreement between the states.

question: Why is 'Insolvency and Bankruptcy' in the concurrent list?
options: Because it is related to banks only
Because only the Center can waive the loan
Because the states do not need this
So that there can be a uniform law for settlement of business loans in the entire country
solution: Entry 9 of the Concurrent List covers this subject, which is of utmost importance for economic reforms.

question: What has been the impact of the 'Anti-Defection Law' (Tenth Schedule)?
options: Stability of governments has increased and 'horse trading' has been curbed
solution: Although this law is also criticized that it suppresses the independent thinking of the members, but it is considered necessary for political stability.

question: What is the function of 'Tribal Advisory Council' mentioned in the Fifth Schedule?
options: Advising the Governor on the welfare of Scheduled Tribes
Sending reports to the Central Government
solution: The Tribal Advisory Council consists of a maximum of 20 members, of whom three-fourths should be representatives of the Scheduled Tribes in the State Assembly.

question: What is the relationship between 'Public Order' and 'Police'?
options: Both are subjects of the State List and complement each other
Public order is a central subject and police is a state subject, both come under the jurisdiction of the state.
Both are in the concurrent list
Police only sees crime, not law
solution: Since law and order is the responsibility of the states, individual states have their own police (e.g. UP Police, Delhi Police - although Delhi is an exception).

question: What is an example of the Indian Constitution being 'flexible'?
options: Formation of new states and change in boundaries by simple majority
Fundamental Rights can never be changed
It is difficult to remove the President
solution: Flexibility ensures that the Constitution does not become irrelevant over time. For example, changing the names of states is a simple legislative act.

question: Why is there no 'strict separation of powers' in India despite having a parliamentary system?
options: Because the President is the head of the Parliament
Because the executive is a part of the legislature
Because the states do not have their own powers
solution: In America the legislature and the executive are completely separate, but in India there is coordination between the two to ensure 'responsive government'.

question: Why has 'Police' been included in the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution?
options: Because the states had demanded it
Because it was the same during the British period, many British traditions have been changed, this has been kept for administrative convenience.
Because maintaining law and order is a local responsibility
solution: Police and public order are the most important subjects in the State List. However, in union territories like Delhi, the police are under the Centre.

question: Which fact is correct regarding the present form of the Indian Constitution?
options: It has more than 448 articles, 25 parts and 12 schedules
It has only 395 Articles and 8 Schedules
It has over 500 articles and 20 schedules
solution: The Indian Constitution is the longest written constitution in the world. Originally it contained 395 articles, 22 parts and 8 schedules. After amendments it currently contains more than 448 articles, 25 parts and 12 schedules.

question: When were 'Maithili' and 'Santhali' added to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
options: By the 21st Amendment, 1967, only Sindhi was added.
solution: The 92nd Amendment further expanded linguistic diversity in the Constitution. This amendment was brought during the Vajpayee government.

question: Who has the power to declare scheduled areas under the Fifth Schedule?
solution: The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration of scheduled areas of other states except Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The President determines these areas.

question: Whose primary responsibility is 'Public Health and Sanitation'?
solution: Public health is mentioned in entry number 6 of the State List of the Seventh Schedule. States decide how they will manage health services.

question: What is the main function of 'Legislature' as a part of government?
solution: There are three organs of government. The legislature makes laws, the executive enacts or enforces them, and the judiciary interprets and judges those laws.

question: Who takes the final decision on disqualification of a member under the Tenth Schedule (D – Defection)?
options: Speaker or Chairman of the House
solution: The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment (1985). This was a drastic step to end the politics of 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram'.

question: How can the 'nature' of the Indian Constitution be explained in one sentence?
options: It is a flexible structure that can be federal or unitary according to circumstances
It is only a group of states
It is only a legal document
It is set in stone that never changes.
solution: The Indian Constitution has preserved India's diversity and successfully governed the world's largest democracy over the last seven decades.

question: What is the position of the states in the 'Quasi-Federal' system?
options: States are highly dependent on the Center but also have their own independent existence
States are like completely independent countries
solution: How. According to Hewer, India is not a federal state but a state with some federal characteristics.

question: What are the residuary powers and who has the right to make laws on them?
options: The President has the authority to give orders
Only states have the right to make laws
Parliament has the authority to make laws on subjects which are not included in the Union, State or Concurrent List.
solution: The doctrine of residual powers is inspired by the Constitution of Canada. In India, under Article 248, the Parliament has the special power to make laws on these subjects.

question: India has taken the parliamentary form of government from the constitution of which country?
solution: India has a parliamentary democracy like Britain. In this, the President is the nominal head and the real powers are vested in the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

question: Which committee made the main recommendation to give constitutional status to 'Panchayati Raj' (Eleventh Schedule)? (PDF Note: General Knowledge)
options: Balwant Rai Mehta and L.M. Singhvi Committee
solution: The 73rd and 74th Amendments attempted to turn Gandhiji's dream of 'Village Swaraj' into reality.

question: By which amendment was the Ninth Schedule added to the Constitution?
solution: The Ninth Schedule was created to abolish Zamindari and remove legal hurdles related to property rights.

question: Why was 'Sanskrit' selected as 'classical language'?
options: Because its literature is very ancient, rich and considered the mother of other languages ​​
Because it is spoken only by Brahmins
Because it is the official official language of India
solution: Sanskrit was given the status of classical language in 2005. It became the second classical language after Tamil (2004).

question: What is an example of 'Education' being in the Concurrent List?
solution: Collaboration between the Center and the State in the field of education is the cornerstone of Indian development.

question: Which language was added by the 21st Constitutional Amendment (1967)?
solution: The process of adding languages ​​to the Eighth Schedule has taken place through amendments from time to time. Sindhi was first added separately.

question: What is the purpose of placing 'Factories' in the Concurrent List?
options: It should be easy to shut down the states
Common law for workers' welfare and industrial development
So that factories are only in cities
solution: Laws like the Factory Act are made by the Centre, but their enforcement is done by state labor departments.

question: How many subjects are currently included in the Union List?
solution: Only the Central Government (Parliament) can make laws on subjects in the Union List. It covers topics of national importance such as defence, atomic energy, foreign affairs and banking.

question: How. How has Hewer described Indian federalism?
solution: Different scholars have interpreted the Indian federal structure differently. How. Hewer called it 'semi-federal' because the unitary features are very dominant in it.
